title: The Little Hermit Crab Who Shared His Shell
titleZh: 把壳借出去的小寄居蟹

illustrations.alt: A sunny shallow sea shore, a little hermit crab named Kai wearing a beautiful pink shell, letting a tiny purple sea anemone named Coral ride on top of his shell, soft waves and starfish around, warm morning light, watercolor illustration style

A big wave sweeping through, the little hermit crab Kai floating without his shell, a blue crab named Bloop holding the borrowed pink shell, a small shrimp and the sea anemone reaching out to help, gentle blue ocean water, watercolor illustration style

An old wise sea turtle pointing with his flipper at a beautiful big spiral shell shining on the ocean floor, friends the little hermit crab, sea anemone, shrimp and blue crab gathered around happily, golden sun rays through clear water, watercolor illustration style

summary: Kai the little hermit crab loves his shiny pink shell more than anything in the sea. So when a homeless sea anemone, a shrimp with a broken shell, and a hurt blue crab all need help, Kai has a big problem — helping them means sharing his precious shell. But when a giant wave sweeps Kai away, the friends he was kind to all come rushing to save him. Kai learns that kindness is like the tide: everything you give out always comes back to you.
moral: Kindness is like the ocean tide — everything you give out comes back to you. A small act of kindness, repeated again and again, makes the whole sea a warmer place. When you help someone find a home, you will never be without one.
moralZh: 善良就像大海的潮水——你付出的每一份善意，都会回到你身边。一个小小的善举，一次又一次地重复，就会让整片大海变得更温暖。当你帮助别人找到家时，你自己永远不会没有家。

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: In a little blue lagoon at the edge of the big ocean, there lived a hermit crab named Kai. On his back he carried a shiny pink shell — smooth, cozy, and just the right size. Kai loved that shell more than anything in the whole sea.

paragraphs.speaker: Kai
paragraphs.text: (polishing his shell with a tiny rag) "Oh, my beautiful shell! You are pink like a sunset and smooth like a dolphin's tummy. Nobody in the lagoon has a shell as lovely as mine."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: One morning, Kai was admiring his shell in the water when he heard a tiny sniffle. It came from a little sea anemone named Coral, who sat alone on a bare rock. Her home — a big rock full of holes — had been broken by last night's storm.

paragraphs.speaker: Coral
paragraphs.text: (wiping her eyes with a tentacle) "Oh dear, oh dear. I have no home anymore. Where will I hide when the big fish swim by? Where will I sleep when the night comes?"

paragraphs.speaker: Kai
paragraphs.text: (looking at his precious shell, then at Coral, then back at his shell) "Well... hmm... my shell is quite small, you know. I don't think there's room for two."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: But Coral looked so sad that Kai's little crab heart went soft. "Wait," he said slowly. "I can't fit you inside. But... you could ride on top! Hold on tight to my shell, and I'll carry you anywhere you need to go." Coral's tentacles wiggled with joy.

paragraphs.speaker: Coral
paragraphs.text: "Really? You would do that for me? Oh, thank you, thank you, Kai! I'll be the best shell-rider in the whole lagoon!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: So Coral climbed up and held on. Together they wobbled across the sand, over pebbles, and past the waving seaweed. Kai felt a funny warm feeling in his chest — like the sun was shining inside him. "Hmm," he whispered. "Helping someone feels... nice."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: The next day, Kai found little Pip the shrimp crying near the shore. Pip's shell had cracked during a game of tag with the waves, and he was too shy to go home with a broken house.

paragraphs.speaker: Pip
paragraphs.text: (sniffling) "I look silly with a crack in my shell. Everyone will laugh at me. What should I do?"

paragraphs.speaker: Kai
paragraphs.text: (thinking of Coral on his back, then nodding) "Come with us, Pip. I know a quiet rock pool where you can rest. And guess what? My shell is big enough for you to hide behind while you heal. We'll be a little shell-bus!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Pip squeezed in behind Kai's shell, and Coral stretched a tentacle to keep him steady. Off they went — a hermit crab, an anemone, and a shrimp, all sharing one little home. The fish in the lagoon watched them pass by and smiled.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: But that night, a blue crab named Bloop came limping out of the dark water. He had bumped into a sharp coral and hurt his leg. "Please," Bloop groaned. "I need shelter for just one night. The tide is coming in, and the current is too strong for me to swim home."

paragraphs.speaker: Kai
paragraphs.text: (his heart racing) "One night? But... my shell is my home! If I give it to you, where will I sleep?" He looked at Coral and Pip, who were both watching him with big, hopeful eyes. Kai took a deep, wobbly breath. "Okay. You can borrow it. Just for one night."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: So Bloop crawled into Kai's precious pink shell, and Kai curled up behind a piece of seaweed, shivering in the cold current. He had no shell. He was just a soft little crab in the wide, dark ocean. He closed his eyes and tried to feel brave. "It's only for one night," he whispered. "One night."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: But the sea is a trickster. At midnight, a giant wave rose up — WHOOSH! — and swept Kai off the sandy floor. He tumbled and tumbled through the dark water, turning round and round like a tiny spinning star, until the wave finally let him go, far, far away from home.

paragraphs.speaker: Kai
paragraphs.text: (floating alone, his voice tiny) "Help! Help! I can't swim back! The shore is too far! And I don't even have my shell..." A big tear mixed with the salty water. "I gave my home away, and now I have nothing."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: But Kai was wrong. Back in the lagoon, Coral felt a strange tug on her tentacles. "Kai is in trouble!" she cried. "I can feel it!" Pip nodded bravely. "Then we're going!" Bloop wiggled out of the pink shell and pushed it along. "That shell belongs to Kai. Let's bring it — and him — home!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: And so the strangest rescue squad in the whole ocean set off: an anemone riding a shrimp, pushing a pink shell through the waves, led by a limping blue crab. They followed the bubbles and the moonlight until they found Kai clinging to a piece of floating wood, tired and cold.

paragraphs.speaker: Coral
paragraphs.text: "Kai! Kai! Hold on to my tentacle! We found you!"

paragraphs.speaker: Bloop
paragraphs.text: (pushing the pink shell toward him) "Here! Your home is back, Kai. Thank you for lending it to me. A crab who lends his shell is the richest crab in the sea."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Kai climbed back into his cozy pink shell and hugged it tight. "Thank you, my friends," he whispered. "I thought kindness made me poor. But look — it brought me back my home, and so many friends besides."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: As they swam home, they met Grandpa Turtle, the oldest creature in the lagoon, gliding slowly through the starlit water. He had seen everything. "Little Kai," he said, his voice warm and deep, "kindness is like the tide. Everything you give out comes back to you — sometimes bigger and more beautiful than before. Follow me."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Grandpa Turtle led them to a secret grotto. And there, shining in a beam of moonlight, lay the most beautiful shell Kai had ever seen — big, smooth, and sparkly, like a piece of the evening sky. "Every time you share your home with someone," Grandpa Turtle smiled, "the sea saves a bigger one for you."

paragraphs.speaker: Kai
paragraphs.text: (his eyes wide with wonder) "For me? But I just helped a few friends. I didn't do anything special." He looked at Coral, Pip, and Bloop, who were all grinning at him. "Oh... I see. You are the ones who helped me. You are my real treasure."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: So Kai moved into his wonderful new shell, and Coral found a soft spot right on top. Pip rode behind, and Bloop walked beside them, his leg all better. From that day on, their little shell-bus traveled the lagoon together, helping anyone who needed a ride, a shelter, or a friend.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Sometimes, when the tide came in and the moon was full, Kai would stop and watch the water. The waves carried shells and sparkles and tiny glowing fish — always giving, always returning. "Kindness is like the tide," he would whisper to his friends. "Give, and the sea will give back."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Good night, little dreamers. Remember Kai the hermit crab, who learned that the warmest home is not made of shells — it is made of friends. When you share a little kindness today, the tide will bring it back to you tomorrow, sparkling like moonlight on the water. Sleep tight, and be kind.
